caveats: **Linux legs are declared CONSTRAINED, and a refused entitlement directory pauses the daily sync.** `pkg_metadata` is a declared-licence classification only (no lapse detection), and whether the agent's account can read `/etc/pki/entitlement` on a real RHEL host is unmeasured. A refused directory or certificate reports `cert_permission_denied` on an authoritative surface, so while it persists the daily `software_licensing` sync skips every cycle (ADR-0024 D3, keep last good) and that host's `pkg_metadata` rows do not land either; an unlistable directory is a refusal for exactly this reason, never an `ok|0` that would replace the stored entitlement records with nothing. That skip rule belongs to the sync source, not to this plugin.

**The entitlement scan's 10 s budget is a start gate, not a deadline.** It is checked before each certificate read; the directory listing comes before it and a read has no deadline of its own, so a certificate reached through a followed link onto a dead network mount can hold the worker for that mount's timeout. There is no mount-table guard because `/etc/pki/entitlement` is a fixed root-owned path on the root filesystem by subscription-manager's contract (the same shape as `runtimes`, #4875).

**macOS yields bundle identity, not licence state.** `vendor_plists` rows are presence-only (status `unknown`) and the Mac App Store receipt (PKCS#7) is not validated, so `mas_receipt` reports a purchase indicator with `Info.plist` identity, never a verified entitlement. An `Info.plist` that is over 4 MiB, unreadable or malformed falls back to the bundle name with an empty version.

**Per-user Windows probes are never a primary surface.** A missing `SeBackup`/`SeRestore` privilege, a refused hive file (the default offline guard, related issue #5291 -- aggregate reason `hive_file_refused`, per-profile sid + specific token logged at `warn`), or a hive-unload failure degrades the `per_user_hives` probe status honestly but never blocks `list` or the daily-sync cycle — per-user licence state is additive, not authoritative.

**An `rpm` execution failure — not absence — falls through to `dpkg-query`.** A stray/leftover `rpm` binary with an uninitialized database (seen live on a self-hosted CI runner) failed every query while `dpkg-query` worked fine as the host's real package manager; only rpm's *absence* is treated as "try the next tool" the same way, execution failure is now handled identically rather than reported as a terminal error. A truncated capture (`output_truncated`) is kept as a distinct, honest failure mode, never folded into a silent partial success.
description: Detects software licences across OS, vendor and per-user surfaces
how_it_works:
Both actions call the same `collect_surfaces()` → `run_platform_surfaces()` per-OS entry point. `list` emits every detected `lic|` record first, then one `probe_status|<surface>|ok|<rows>` (or `|error|<message>`) diagnostic line per surface attempted, then returns rc 0 unconditionally — "success" is structural (the enumeration sweep completed), not a claim that every surface answered. `surfaces` runs the identical sweep but suppresses the `lic|` records, emitting only the `probe_status|` diagnostics; it is the live-diagnostics counterpart to `list`, not a cheaper version of it.

Per OS, surfaces run in a fixed order, most-authoritative first: Windows queries WMI `SoftwareLicensingProduct` (`slp_wmi`, authoritative licence state), then Office ClickToRun config, then the machine-scope `ProbeSpec` table rows (SQL Server, Exchange, VMware, WinRAR, OSS presence, …), then per-user registry hives and profile files. Linux runs `pkg_metadata` (rpm, falling back to dpkg-query), then RHEL `entitlement_certs` (the directory listed and each certificate read and parsed in-process via libcrypto, authoritative expiry; a directory or certificate the agent may not read is `cert_permission_denied`, never an empty surface), then FlexLM `.lic` files. macOS runs the Mac App Store receipt scan (bundle identity from `Info.plist`, XML or binary), then vendor-plist presence rows.

The plugin is deliberately not an entitlement tracker: FlexLM seat counts and KMS activation counts (`ent|` records) are explicit PR2 scope (ADR-0024 D12) and are never emitted here; emitting them needs that decision revisited. It is also not a general plist parser — a binary (`bplist00`) `Info.plist` is read by a bounded, plugin-local decoder that returns only the top-level `CFBundleDisplayName`, `CFBundleName` and `CFBundleShortVersionString` strings, and a plist that cannot be decoded falls back to the bundle name with an empty version.
name: license_scan
outputs_note: No definition YAML ships for this plugin, so these tables are derived from the plugin source and the sample captures rather than `spec.result.columns`. `list` emits two distinct row shapes on the same stream: `lic|` records (one per detected licence) followed by `probe_status|` diagnostics (one per surface attempted); `surfaces` emits only the `probe_status|` diagnostics. Every `lic` field is drawn from a closed vocabulary and is "unknown-preserving" — the plugin never fabricates a value it cannot justify; absence is empty, not a guess.

privileges.grant: **None.** Machine-scope surfaces need only the agent account's existing registry-read access. The per-user offline-hive fallback rides `SeBackupPrivilege` + `SeRestorePrivilege`, already held by the agent account for `tar.*`/certificate-store writes — no new privilege is introduced.
privileges.if_refused: `slp_wmi` (authoritative) errors block the daily-sync cycle; `per_user_hives` degrades to `privilege_missing`/`hive_file_refused`/`hive_unload_failed`/`profile_list_truncated` without blocking `list`, since per-user hives are never a primary surface -- `hive_file_refused` is the aggregate reason when the default offline hive-file guard (related issue #5291) refuses any profile's hive; the per-profile sid and the guard's specific token go to the agent log at `warn`, never into the row itself

privileges.grant: **None.** `mas_receipt`/`vendor_plists` are unprivileged filesystem glob + plist reads (`/Applications/*.app/Contents/Info.plist` is world-readable).
privileges.if_refused: no coded refusal path: an absent glob match reports a structural zero-row success, never an error, and an `Info.plist` that cannot be read or decoded falls back to the bundle name with an empty version
privileges.measured: 2026-10-26, bare-metal, at euid 501 (unprivileged) — this plugin needs none of the daemon's root grant
privileges.runs_as: agent LaunchDaemon, runs as **root** today (no `UserName` key; required for TAR's Endpoint Security client, unrelated to this plugin)

privileges.grant: **None for `pkg_metadata` and FlexLM `.lic` files** (rpm/dpkg-query and the conventional `.lic` directories are world-readable). **RHEL entitlement certificates under `/etc/pki/entitlement/` are not assumed readable:** subscription-manager creates them root-owned and the unprivileged account's access is **UNMEASURED** on a real RHEL host (none has been measured).
privileges.if_refused: `entitlement_certs` reports `cert_permission_denied` (result status `PERMISSION_DENIED`) when the directory cannot be listed or a certificate cannot be read — never `ok|0`; an unlistable directory for another reason, an oversized or unparseable certificate reports `cert_parse_failed`/`cert_parse_partial`; a truncated listing, more than 64 certificate files or more than 16 certificates in one file reports `cert_scan_budget_exhausted`; `pkg_metadata` reports `dpkg_query_failed`/`output_truncated` on a query failure
privileges.measured: 2026-09-06, container, at euid 0 (root) — not representative of the unprivileged production account, and the entitlement directory was absent there, so the RHEL grant is unmeasured
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon, designed to run unprivileged as `yuzu`

result_status.when: every probe outcome in the run was `ok` — the case in all three sample captures

the `entitlement_certs` outcome is `cert_permission_denied` (the agent may not list `/etc/pki/entitlement` or read a certificate in it); takes precedence over `CONSTRAINED`, set identically after both `list` and `surfaces`; rows already collected are kept
at least one probe surface outcome has `ok=false` and none is a permission refusal, set identically after both `list` and `surfaces`

where_the_data_goes: **Daily-sync (`software_licensing` source).** `list` output feeds a 24 h scheduled sync: the empty-vs-error structural guard skips a cycle (keeps last good state) if a primary/authoritative surface (`slp_wmi`, `entitlement_certs`, `flexlm_lic`) errored — `cert_permission_denied` included — and caps at 10,000 records / 1 MiB blob / 2 MiB raw capture — an over-cap or over-budget cycle is skipped rather than sent truncated.
**Server store.** The blob is parsed and ingested into `SoftwareLicensingStore`.

**REST.** `GET /api/v1/sle/agents/{agent_id}` — per-device detected licences (product, type, channel, state, expiry, confidence, exe_hints, and the per-user `user_scope`/`user_ref` fields), gated `SoftwareLicensing:Read` scoped to the device, audited per open. `DELETE /api/v1/sle/agents/{agent_id}` — decommission erasure, requiring `SoftwareLicensing:Delete` AND `Inventory:Delete` AND `GuaranteedState:Delete`.
**MCP.** The `query_software_licenses` tool, gated `SoftwareLicensing:Read`, confined scope — reads the same store, not a live dispatch.
**Not consumed by** the TAR warehouse or DEX/metrics pipelines — no reference to `license_scan` or `SoftwareLicensing` was found in those paths in this sweep.

**Sensitivity.** `lic` rows are an installed-software/licence inventory: `product`/`vendor`/`version` name specific installed software and versions, `exe_hints` names installed executables, and `key_hint` carries a partial OS-provided key or key-derived hash (never raw key material); `user_scope`/`user_ref` can carry a local profile name for a user-scoped licence (empty in every sample capture here). `probe_status` rows carry nothing beyond a surface name and row count.
**Siblings:** none shipped. `ent|` entitlement records (FlexLM seat counts, KMS activation counts) are explicitly out of scope for this plugin (PR2, ADR-0024 D12) — see Caveats.

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) → `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) → `discover_instructions` finds no definition for this plugin today — no `content/definitions/license_scan.yaml` exists, so `get_definition(...)` has no id to resolve. Run: once an `InstructionDefinition` is authored against `license_scan.list`/`license_scan.surfaces`, `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `GET /api/v1/sle/agents/{agent_id}` or the MCP `query_software_licenses` tool.
